name: Sceilg Mhichíl
description: Skellig Michael is a jagged twin-peaked rock rising 218 metres from the Atlantic, about 12 km off County Kerry's Iveragh Peninsula. Monks built a monastery here between the 6th and 8th centuries, high above the waves and reached by steep, narrow stone steps. Its remarkably well-preserved buildings share the island with gannets, puffins and grey seals, and visits are possible only in summer.
